A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from MuseRAG to MuseScorer. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational evaluations and psychometric analyses of existing AUT datasets, including human agreement, validity correlations, and robustness results.

after.justification: v2 reports original MuseScorer evaluations, including model comparisons, validity correlations, and robustness analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.3 retain the same incremental retrieval, LLM bucketing decisions, codebook updates, and prompt contents. MuseRAG becomes MuseScorer, and baseline prompting becomes vanilla prompting; the expanded architecture explanation does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use socialmuse24, beaty18, silvia17, beaty12, and mohr16 with identical AUT coverage and Table 1 counts. The added dataset examples and annotation distinctions describe existing coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2, A4, and A5 retain the same LLM configurations and K-means/agglomerative comparisons using Silhouette and Semantic criteria. Newly discussed creativity-scoring methods in Section 2 are citations, not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sample counts, model sizes, evaluation metrics, baseline cluster-count searches, and the default Kc = 10 with checks at 5 and 15 remain unchanged. Less specific judge and embedding descriptions do not establish an alternative experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Section 7.6 retains the same configuration comparisons, retrieval-size checks, ordering tests, and originality-metric analyses. Human-annotator comparisons and distributional analyses in the appendices are also unchanged; no new robustness experiment or error analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same confidence-interval practices, significance tests, Bland–Altman limits, and three random-order seeds. Table 3 and the redesigned Figure 2 redisplay existing statistical information.

E6.justification: Matched numerical entries in Table 2 and Tables A1–A5 are unchanged. v2's Table 3 reproduces v1 Section 7.5 correlations, and Figure 2 already showed the same bias of -1.42 and agreement limits of -2.94 and 0.09 in v1. Appendix plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same partition and frequency definitions, four originality formulas, and normalization. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The automation and psychometric-validity claims remain. The conclusion narrows the interpretability claim from providing justifications for each originality score to providing justifications for bucketing decisions, aligning the stated contribution more closely with the prompt outputs.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 explicitly identifies the secondary datasets' lack of human bucketing annotations, and Limitations adds erroneous bucket assignments as a hallucination risk. Section 6.1 also changes 'fat-tailed' to 'scale-free,' despite retaining Section 5.1's qualification against a strict power-law interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 7.1 drops the explicit statement that baselines use the same embedding alternatives, and Section 3.2 removes the specification of averaging three mohr16 judges. The printed repository name changes to MuseScorer. Appendix A.1–A.3 otherwise retain the models, prompts, hardware, and approximately 100 GPU days.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds Chakrabarty et al. (2024) and Lu et al. (2024), distinguishing direct LLM creativity ratings and corpus-similarity approaches from intent-sensitive bucketing. v2 also adds Chakrabarty et al. (2025) and removes the Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion comparison.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, dataset descriptions, prototype narrative, conclusion, and limitations undergo extensive rewriting. Section 7.5 replaces dense numerical prose with a table-referencing narrative, while system and prompting terminology changes throughout.

P2.justification: New Table 3 consolidates existing prose results. Figure 2 becomes larger with an external legend and revised axis typography, while Tables 2 and A5 explicitly group MuseScorer configurations and baselines. These are localized display changes; appendix plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: Table 3, the more legible Figure 2, and clearer method explanations make the existing evidence easier to assess. The revised interpretability claim and explicit validation boundaries improve precision. Reduced specificity in some experimental descriptions and the loose new 'scale-free' wording partly offset these gains, leaving a modest overall improvement.
